title: Conclusion: eternal mind — God is
source_text: XLII. Itaque concludimus integrum hoc universum, & singula quae in eo observantur a se ipsis non esse, sed sui causam aliquam habere: causam autem illam esse non posse casum & fortunam, nec etiam naturam quandam caecam & sui nesciam, sed necessario esse mentem aeternam, optimam, potentissimam, & sapientissimam, quam Deum appellamus. Et sic existimamus, quod nobis propositum erat, nos evidenter demonstrasse, nimirum Deum esse.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore we conclude that this entire universe, and the singular things observed in it, are not from themselves, but have some cause of themselves: but that that cause cannot be chance and fortune, nor even some blind nature ignorant of itself, but must necessarily be an eternal mind, best, most powerful, and wisest, which we call God. And so we judge that what had been proposed to us, we have evidently demonstrated, namely that God is.
pass_b_english: Universe and its parts are not a-se — they need a cause.
Not chance, not blind self-ignorant nature.
Necessary: eternal mind, best, strongest, wisest — God. Demonstratum: God is.
